title: 374. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Slope of a Line Through Two Points
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Compute rise divided by run between two points.
questions.question: What is the slope of the line through \((1,3)\) and \((5,11)\)?
questions.hint: Put the change in the vertical coordinate in the numerator.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate slope when vertical coordinates decrease.
questions.question: What is the slope of the line through \((-2,5)\) and \((4,-7)\)?
questions.hint: Keep the same endpoint order in both coordinate differences.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the slope of a horizontal line.
questions.question: What is the slope of the line through \((-3,4)\) and \((6,4)\)?
questions.explanation: The rise is zero and the run is \(9\). Thus the slope is \(\frac{0}{9}=0\).
questions.hint: Check whether the rise or the run is zero.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish undefined slope from zero slope.
questions.question: What is the slope of the line through \((2,-5)\) and \((2,7)\)?
questions.explanation: The run is zero while the rise is \(12\). The quotient \(\frac{12}{0}\) is undefined.
questions.hint: Inspect the denominator in the slope formula.

questions.question: What is the slope of the line through \((-1,-2)\) and \((3,1)\)?
questions.hint: Distinguish rise over run from its reciprocal.

questions.learningObjective: Compute slope consistently when endpoints are listed in reverse direction.
questions.question: What is the slope of the line through \((3,8)\) and \((-1,0)\)?
questions.explanation: Using the listed order gives \(\frac{0-8}{-1-3}=\frac{-8}{-4}=2\). Reversing both differences preserves the slope.
questions.hint: Two negative coordinate differences can give a positive slope.

questions.learningObjective: Recover a coordinate from a specified line slope.
questions.question: The line through \((0,4)\) and \((6,t)\) has slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\). What is \(t\)?
questions.hint: Convert the slope into a required vertical change.

questions.learningObjective: Solve for a horizontal coordinate in the slope formula.
questions.question: The line through \((a,2)\) and \((5,8)\) has slope \(3\). What is \(a\)?
questions.hint: Determine the run that corresponds to the given rise and slope.

questions.concept: Using slope to predict a coordinate
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a new vertical coordinate from a horizontal change.
questions.question: A line has slope \(\frac{1}{3}\) and passes through \((2,-1)\). What is the vertical coordinate of its point with horizontal coordinate \(11\)?
questions.explanation: The horizontal change is \(9\), so the vertical change is \(\frac{1}{3}\cdot9=3\). The required coordinate is \(-1+3=2\).
questions.hint: Multiply the horizontal change by the slope.

questions.learningObjective: Recover a parameter by equating successive slopes.
questions.question: The three points \((1,2)\), \((4,8)\), and \((7,k)\) are collinear. What is \(k\)?
questions.explanation: The first segment has slope \(\frac{6}{3}=2\). Thus \(\frac{k-8}{3}=2\), giving \(k=14\).
questions.hint: Collinear points share the same line slope.
